messages:
lily: Hey team — onboarding hiccup. On my M2 Mac I installed node via asdf (nodejs 18) but npm install fails with node-gyp complaining about OpenSSL. Also trying to get SSH agent forwarding/keys sorted for private repo clones. Anyone seen this?

devon: hi! for node-gyp it's usually OpenSSL headers. Also double-check asdf shims are first in your PATH so the node you expect is used. What exact error do you see?

lily: npm ERR! gyp ERR! stack Error: Can't find OpenSSL include directory.

samir: Try installing brew openssl and set flags when building native deps. For example:
```bash
brew install openssl@1.1
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
# then reinstall node modules or run 
npm rebuild
asdf reshim nodejs
```
That usually fixes node-gyp on Apple Silicon.

lily: thanks! Where should I put those exports? .zprofile or .zshrc? I'm on zsh.

maria: put persistent envs in ~/.zprofile for login shells (homebrew on mac usually needs that). For interactive stuff .zshrc is fine. Also make sure you source asdf early so shims are in PATH. Example snippet to add to ~/.zprofile:
```bash
# Homebrew on Apple Silicon
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
# OpenSSL for native builds
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
# asdf
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
. $HOME/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash
```
That ordering helps asdf+brew play nicely.

lily: also my SSH agent isn't forwarding when I try to jump through a host to clone our private repo. I added key with ssh-add but `ssh -T git@github.com` still asks for passphrase.

devon: mac quirks — use the keychain flags. Try `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (or `ssh-add -K` on older macOS). And ensure ~/.ssh/config has:
```
Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```
Then restart the terminal, add the key once, it should persist.

lily: added that and restarted — `ssh -T git@github.com` now says Hi! :tada:

lily: one more thing — our repo uses the osx credential helper but git still prompts for creds occasionally. How do I configure credential helper properly?

samir: run `git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`. If you installed git via brew, make sure brew/git is earlier in PATH (so `git --version` shows the brew one). Also run `git credential-osxkeychain store` once when prompted. If you still get prompts, check Keychain Access for stale entries and remove them.

lily: sweet, that sorted it. Final Q: for dotfiles — should I fork the org dotfiles or use the template? Where's the onboarding dotfiles instruction?

maria: Welcome! We have a starter dotfiles repo in the org and a short onboarding doc (I'll DM you the link). Ping me and I'll add you to the repo so you can clone it. Also add REPO_TOKEN and REDWOOD_DEV env vars to your ~/.zprofile (we use them for some internal tooling).

infra-bot: Reminder: new-hire office hours Wednesday 10:00am PT — join if you want live help with setup. :calendar:

lily: thanks everyone, super helpful. I'll clean up the installs and post any follow-ups here.
